last_outcome: P9.3 multi-Y terrain — `src/world/village.ts` `addHills(grid, seed, treeCells, reservedCells?, count=3)` stamps 3 elevated 5x5 mini-hills onto the outskirts via mulberry32(seed+9001). Each hill cell becomes VOXEL_DIRT at y=0 (slope substrate) + VOXEL_FLOOR grass cap at y=1. Rejection rules per spec: centre within PLAZA_HALF+5=15 of plaza, within PATH_HALF+3=6 of either road centreline, within 3 of tavern footprint, within 4 of any tree (all Chebyshev). Additional safety: the 5x5 footprint must currently be plain grass (y=0=FLOOR + y=1=EMPTY) so hills don't clobber ponds/roads/plaza/buildings or anything already stacked at y=1; reserved cells (NPCs + items + trees passed in from main.ts) are excluded from the footprint so existing scene-objects don't get sunk into the new cap. Hills also reject overlap with each other (Chebyshev <= HILL_HALF*2+1=5). `src/entities/player.ts` swaps the old `hitsWall(x,z)` boolean for `resolveFloor(x, z, fromFloor) -> number` that returns the cell-layer Y the player would occupy (= top of surface), or -1 if blocked. Algorithm: scan range capped at `fromFloor` so overhead structures (market-stall canopy at y=3) don't inflate the surface height; pick highest non-empty voxel in [1, fromFloor] across footprint, newFloor = topSolidY + 1. Step-up capped at STEP_UP_MAX=1 vs fromFloor (so tavern walls + stall posts at y=1,2 still block — newFloor jumps to 3, diff > 1). Step-down unlimited (no gravity — player snaps to whatever's below). Head clearance: cell at newFloor must be empty across the footprint, so walking into a 2-tall wall (y=1+y=2 solid) is blocked even though step-up math would otherwise allow it (newFloor=2, cell y=2 = wall -> blocked). Legacy VOXEL_WALL at y=0 stays unconditionally blocking. New `Player.snapToFloor()` recomputes floor + sets mesh.y after any external position write (save restore, test movePlayerTo). `currentFloorY` tracked as instance state (initial GROUND_FLOOR_Y=1). `src/main.ts` restructured: NPC/item/foliage placement runs first (against flat ground), THEN addHills mutates the grid with reservedCells = NPC+item+tree cells, THEN buildVoxelMesh + scene.add (so rendered geometry includes the caps). Player creation stays before hills (only stores a grid reference); `snapToFloor()` called once post-hills so save-restored XZ on a hill cell raises the player onto the cap. New test hooks: getPlayerY, getHillCount, getHillPositions; movePlayerTo now snaps floor after warp. `scripts/validate-visual.mjs` P9.3 block asserts hills >= 1, warps to first hill centre via movePlayerTo, waits 200ms for camera follow, asserts getPlayerY rose by >= 0.5 vs flat-ground baseline, captures iter-${ITER}-hill.png, warps back to plaza centre and asserts Y snapped back to baseline +-0.1. Build green 545.78 kB (+1.88 kB vs iter 53's 543.90 kB — addHills source + resolveFloor/snapToFloor player methods + test hooks).
